sourcedFrom: Ruger RXM Centerfire Pistol Instruction Manual — PM1183 (2026)
cleanIntro: The RXM requires the trigger to be pulled before the slide will come off. Everything before that step exists to make that safe.

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Keep the pistol pointed in a safe direction, press down on the magazine release and remove the magazine.
steps.prose: Feeding source out before anything else moves.
steps.quote: Keep the pistol pointed in a safe direction. Press down on the magazine release and remove the magazine
steps.cite: Ruger RXM Centerfire Pistol Instruction Manual — PM1183 — Disassembly, step 1, p.22
steps.warn: Always unload a firearm before cleaning, lubrication, disassembly, or assembly.

steps.title: Lock the slide open
steps.action: Pull the slide to the rear and lock it open by pushing upward on the slide stop.
steps.prose: Locked back is what lets you see and feel the chamber properly.
steps.quote: Pull the slide to the rear and lock it in the open position by pushing upward on the slide stop.
steps.cite: Ruger RXM Centerfire Pistol Instruction Manual — PM1183 — Disassembly, step 2, p.22

steps.title: Verify the chamber
steps.action: Inspect the chamber and verify that it is empty.
steps.prose: By sight and by finger. This is the check the next step depends on.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber and verify that it is empty
steps.cite: Ruger RXM Centerfire Pistol Instruction Manual — PM1183 — Disassembly, step 3, p.22

steps.title: Let the slide forward
steps.action: Retract the slide slightly and release it.
steps.prose: That short pull drops the slide stop out of the way.
steps.quote: This will disengage the slide stop and allow the slide to move fully forward.
steps.cite: Ruger RXM Centerfire Pistol Instruction Manual — PM1183 — Disassembly, step 4, p.22

steps.title: Point safe and pull the trigger
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction and pull the trigger to the rear.
steps.prose: This design will not release the slide until the striker is down. You cleared the chamber twice above; that is why this is safe.
steps.quote: Point the pistol in a safe direction and pull the trigger to the rear
steps.cite: Ruger RXM Centerfire Pistol Instruction Manual — PM1183 — Disassembly, step 5, p.23
steps.warn: This is the step where negligent discharges happen when the chamber check is skipped. If the pistol left your hands at any point, clear it again before pulling the trigger.

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame — and if it hangs up
steps.action: Draw the slide back slightly, hold the takedown lever down and run the slide forward off the frame. If it hangs up, pull the trigger a second time.
steps.prose: Ruger documents that hang-up: the trigger or connector can reset while the slide is pulled rearward, and a second trigger pull frees it.
steps.quote: If this occurs, pull the trigger a second time, which should allow the slide to move freely off the frame.
steps.cite: Ruger RXM Centerfire Pistol Instruction Manual — PM1183 — Disassembly, step 6 note, p.23

deepAbsentReason: PM1183 documents the field strip only — slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly off the frame. No detail strip past that is published, so this listing has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent patch, correctly sized brush, then dry patches until clean
Wipe the feed ramp and chamber mouth

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Scrub the breech face and around the extractor
Wipe the striker channel DRY — no oil in an ignition channel
One drop of oil on each slide rail

cleaning.name: FRAME & MAGAZINES
tasks: Brush the frame rails and the magazine well
Clean all magazine components with a brush or rag to remove residue
Reassemble magazines in reverse order, taking care the spring goes in the correct orientation

reassembly: Seat the barrel and recoil spring assembly in the slide.
Run the slide onto the frame rails and rack it fully — it locks in automatically.
fncheck: With the magazine out and chamber confirmed empty, rack the slide several times and confirm the trigger resets, pointed in a safe direction.
